sentences.text: This meeting is being recorded.
Hello, Andy, how are you?

Okay, brilliant.

I don't know how much you know or where you came across capital A or agencies go.
We're an M and A advisory, we work just with marketing services.
So all of our clients are either buyers or sellers or marketing agencies.
Some of those on the buy side tend to be PE or investors, investment groups and companies.
But mostly it's agencies looking for high growth.
And on the sell side we have agencies co, which is our marketplace for agency owners to buy and sell their businesses.
So yeah, we're mostly probably based in the US about 90% of the time.
And the rest is, I would say, sort of Middle east, some in Asia, Middle East, Mediterranean, you know, Europe, those types of places with the occasional Australian one as well.
So it's fairly global.
But I would say our focus is US based.
So it'd be great to really get into what it is that you're looking to do.
Obviously we'd be keen to help you if you're looking to Sell.
So um, yeah.
What what is it exactly that you're planning to do at the moment and why.
Yeah, yeah.
So are you guys similar to like Merge.com?
Yeah, very similar.
I guess in a lot of ways I think their focus is, is more about being a broker whereas we, we are definitely both sides of, of the table.
So we buy a lot as well as, as working on the sell side.
So possibly slightly different networks but, but yeah, similar in a lot of ways as well.
Both in the same space.
I see.
Yeah.
So I'll just run out about our company, a little bit of history and what I'm looking at the moment.
So we are a influencer agency.
So I, I started the agency in 2020 actually late late of 2020 during COVID It was pretty serendipitous because I, I wasn't planning on going into this industry.

I was in the Internet industry so I was helping startups to expand to different global go to markets at the time I exit my previous company and seeing the pandemic so I pretty much don't have a lot of things to do and I just came across an opportunity to provide influencers to, to one of the video content platforms originally from China that they are expanding overseas.
So they are kind at the time they were like a competitor of TikTok.
So at that time I, I, I become a vendor to help them to outreach influencers, bring them onto their platform.

So that's how we started and we did pretty good for that project and then we had another project for their latam operation and then we got some traction from some brands saying hey, they know that we are working with influencers so they wanted to see if we can help with our campaigns.
So initially mostly brands from China that they wanted to penetrate global market, us, Europe, Southeast Asia, whatnot.
So we slowly pivot our main business into helping brands to, to strategize and execute influencer campaigns.

So we, we work with both, we work with like almost all regions except for mainland China because they have different social media but we, we, we help with mostly landing social campaigns on YouTube, Instagram, TikTok and yeah 90% of them are based in Asia.
We do have some clients once in a while western clients that are looking to do business with us as well.
For example, we had a Israeli company, a gaming publisher that they wanted to do campaigns in Brazil so we helped with them for a few campaigns because we do have local team member in Brazil.
We also helped some US education tech companies to do campaigns in Southeast Asia and yeah, so so in A nutshell, that's what we do.
And for me, Well, I own 100 of the company, so I don't have, I, I, I bootstrap from the very beginning.
I don't have any investors.
And yeah, like starting from our first year, we, we are net positive.
So our revenue was always growing and we were always net positive.
And I'm looking to sell my company next year.
The reason being that my passion is more about from 0 to 1.
My passion is more about scaling, building something from scratch.
And I pretty much stumbled upon this opportunity.
And because we have a remote global team, so our operation cost is pretty low and we have very strong SOPs in place.
So we're very strong in terms of influencer execution.

And so we started to realize that we might be a good target for potential buyers that are looking to acquire agency with a lot of client portfolio in Asia, or they're looking for agency that have a strong influencer execution pipeline and also a system where we can deploy campaigns or scale teams rapidly because we have team members all over the place and it's easy for us to, to scale a new team from scratch relatively fast.
Okay, cool.
So founded in California, but mostly working with Asian clients.
And your team is across the globe, but with a focus and concentration around Asia as well.
And so obviously are you American or what should I say?
I'm a U.S. citizen.
I was born in China and I have a US Citizen now.
And finally you mentioned it because now I, because of the tax reason.
So I intentionally not don't stay in US for extended period of time just to take advantage of foreign earned income exclusion.
And because my US entity is owned 100% by my belief LLC, so I'm effectively a employee of my US entity, so that does help me to save some taxes.
So unless necessary, I seldom go back to US or if I need to be in that time zone, I restate in Canada or Mexico.
Okay, all right.
Yeah, well, that's the options nowadays.
Yeah.
And a lot of my team members, they also take liberty of our structure.
So a lot of them are digital nomads.
And the, that's why we have a very strong retention, you know, in terms of agency.
So like for example, this year we, we only had one person leave and other, other team members left were because of our company decision.
So, so the what, what size is your team?
30 people.
Did you say 30?
Yeah.
Yeah.
So very stable team.
Yeah.
And in terms of your revenue, you said you've always been profit profitable.
You're currently at $4 million in revenue with a 10% margin, is that correct?
Yeah, last year we did 3.5.
This year we are looking between 4 to 5.
Yeah.
And this is a gross revenue.
So that including like, let's say if we sell a package to a client for like 250k, that including the crater cost.
So.
Yeah.
One second.

It.

No problem.

About an hour and 20 minutes outside of London.

Yeah.
Okay.

Right.

Get my breath back.

Yeah, last year, Last year we did.
Let me see.

So usually our first half it's not very high because we kind of reinvest into our team.
Usually we make up the net income towards the end of the year, especially when we get more, more of our campaign payments back.
This year we are looking at something similar.

So.
And also coming to the.

And so in that case I might, starting from end of this year I might trim and optimize our team a little bit so that our net margin could increase compared to the last few years.
But what that will mean is that our revenue might stagnate a little bit.
Yeah.
Okay.
But yeah, it's about maximizing your valuation.

Yeah.

That's all good.
Yeah.

If we're looking at the revenue multiple, I'm looking at 1x.

We, we were cash positive from the first year.

So our team is rather flexible in terms of post acquisition.

Yeah.
Okay, so 8x and do you have any sort of IP in the business at all?
Is there anything that is uniquely yours, whether it's tech or process or anything like that?
I wouldn't say tech because we use, well, we use a lot of tech.
We work with a lot of AI companies and we work with a lot of tech.

Yeah, I mean it is nothing that's Patented, but it works pretty well and is very efficient for our team.
Okay, cool.
Yeah.
Right.
Okay.
And then.
So why are you here now?
What's the conversation that we're having?
What's that about?

So I guess right now could be the time to get prepared for that.
So that's why I got your email.
So I'm actually in talk with several agencies or brokers that are in the M and A field.

Yeah.
Yeah, so.

So I'm pretty confident that AX is probably at the top end of the spectrum for what you could get.
I mean, there is definitely a lot of interest in influencer agencies and they're valued higher than normal agencies.
So if you had two agencies next to each other and one did digital marketing and one did influencer, the influencer one would definitely be worth more for sure.
Obviously there's a ton of other factors that influence whether a company is a certain value or not.
But certainly just comparing like, for, like influencer agencies are worth more the range of value for a business your size.
And you did say like a gross revenue, so it's kind of overestimated slightly, but just on the top end.
But you know, for that sort of level of EBITDA, we would say about 20%.
So let's say you are doing about 200 million in net revenue.
Sorry, 2 million in net revenue.
Then a business that size is probably somewhere in the region of sort of three to five times ebitda.
Given a premium for it being an influencer agency, it could be somewhere in the region of four to six times multiple.
So I would say at the top end of that scale, we're probably looking at a 6x and 8x would be toppy in terms of growth.

And so you could be closer to whatever your target is.
But I would just say as a sort of very rough estimation without looking into your books, that that's kind of the, the ballpark that I would put you at.
And I'm aware that a lot of our competitors that you may have spoke to already will, they will try and get a deal by overpricing agencies.
But you know, the reality is even if we listed the business higher than what it is, we're only going to get offers that are around the sensible valuations.
And so I would say the top end of that sort of three to five.
Sorry, I froze.
You froze.

So start to finish, we're looking to get the business sold within that six month window.

You know, sometimes it does take more work to find the right buyer and quite often we can find a lot of buyers in the, in the first 24 hours.
So it really does depend, I would say possibly because you guys are mostly Chinese in terms of where your work falls, we possibly wouldn't have the strongest network for that.
Most of our buyers are American and most of them are looking for the easiest route.
So they're looking to buy American business.

So to me, exactly like you said, so to me, I think the best synergy would be a potential buyer that's looking to acquire company that have a strong clientele in Asia that and also happen to appreciate what we have in terms of our remote team, our systematic sops, our influencer execution capacity.
So if it's just for our profitability and our revenue, I don't think that the potential buyer will justify a higher multiple.

Yeah.

Yeah.

I mean.
Right.

Is it.

I don't.
I don' overhead for.

Yeah, yeah.

December, of course, slow, January is slow.
Maybe the third or fourth week of January it starts to pick back up.

So I'd say we are currently in an active period.
And then there's another one starting in February.

Okay, cool.

You too.

Cheers.

summary.overview:
- Thomas Huang's influencer marketing agency generated $3.5M in revenue last year and targets $4-5M for this year, indicating strong growth potential.
- The agency's net owner discretionary income is approximately $380K, providing a solid financial base for valuation discussions.
- Thomas seeks to achieve an 8x net income or 1x revenue multiple upon sale, backed by consistent profitability and effective influencer systems.
- Operational efficiency is highlighted by strong proprietary SOPs, making the agency attractive for integrated marketing groups focused on Asian market entry.
- M&A advisory discussions are underway as Thomas plans for a projected sale next year, considering multiple brokerage options.
- Typical valuation multiples for influencer agencies are communicated as ranging from 4x to 6x EBITDA, emphasizing market standards.
- The agency's US registration in Wyoming is positioned as a strategic advantage for attracting US buyers, aligning with its unique clientele.
- The M&A process is estimated to take about 6 months from preparation to closing, with varying activity levels throughout the year.
- Initial outreach for M&A services starts strongly from September to November, with an anticipated slowdown in December and January.
- Proposed fees for advisory services are $30,000 for a full process and around $10,750 for a lighter version, with Thomas eager to review options.
summary.short_summary: Thomas's influencer agency, founded in late 2020, has established a strong foothold in the global market, primarily serving Asian clients with an emphasis on social media platforms like YouTube and Instagram. The company operates as a US-registered LLC with a remote team and has shown consistent annual revenue growth, projected to reach between $4 million to $5 million this year. Valuation discussions indicate a target of 8x net income, although market insights suggest a more realistic range of 4x to 6x EBITDA for similar agencies. The agency's unique blend of Asian market expertise and Western operational culture positions it well for buyers seeking scalable and flexible operations. Thomas plans to exit the business next year to pursue new ventures, emphasizing the importance of selecting the right buyer to maximize the agency's valuation.
